analysis.title: Bath & Body Works Inc. (BBWI) 3Q26 Recap: Underlying business trends remain pressured; tariffs and oil costs to weigh on 4Q gross margins
key_insights: BBWI closed up 1.3% on 11/19 versus the S&P down 2.0% after its 3Q beat and FY26 top line guidance raise. Store traffic stayed pressured and body care came in below management expectations.

GS reiterates Sell. The company is in an investment year and the underlying business remains under pressure. GS does not expect a return to growth this year and sees brand sentiment among younger consumers taking time to improve.

3Q sales were $1,577mn, above FactSet consensus of $1,551mn, and down 1.1% y/y. That is better than the 2Q decline of 2.3%. Traffic was a headwind, particularly late in the quarter, as inflation weighed on consumers and competition in core categories intensified.

By category, soaps and sanitizers grew low single digits, led by sanitizers. Home fragrance was roughly flat, with single and four-wick candles, Wallflowers and concentrated room sprays growing. Growth in new and existing franchises was offset by a decline in Halloween seasonal products.

Body care (~37% of FY25 North America sales) performed well below company expectations, with high-single-digit sales declines similar to 2Q. Management cited weak Halloween and seasonal products and heavier competition from rivals expanding into seasonal collections and fragrance-led storytelling.

New franchises are getting a positive response. Over 50% of Essentials (launched Sept 2026) customers returned within 30 days. Everyday Luxuries retail sales doubled y/y after the relaunch. The Reserve four-wick candle (launched Aug 2026) is seeing repeat purchases above the company benchmark.
Increased marketing spend, including celebrity partnerships and paid traditional and social media, produced improving trends from new, existing and reactivated customers, particularly in digital.

Amazon and Ulta are building momentum. Bath & Body Works will launch Pink Suede exclusively at Ulta and expand from ~600 to ~1,500 Ulta stores. Amazon data shows the company winning back lost share, at a materially higher AUR than its own channels. Both channels are expected to grow sequentially in 4Q.

4Q guidance has net sales declining 5.5% to 2.0% versus consensus of -2.1%, a sequential worsening, on a smaller wholesale lift and a pressured, competitive consumer environment. The high end implies North America retail sales roughly flat versus 3Q.
4Q gross margin faces pressure from incremental Canadian tariffs (over 100bps), higher crude oil costs (~100bps) and buying and occupancy deleverage on lower sales and real estate investment.

GS estimate changes: FY26 sales growth held at -2.9%, gross margin cut to 42.7% from 43.3%, SG&A ratio to 29.4% from 29.6%. FY26 EPS falls 2.5% to $2.67 from $2.73. FY27 and FY28 EPS rise 3.5% and 3.6% to $2.69 and $2.95. FY29 EPS introduced at $3.23. Estimates include the $80mn tariff refund benefit received in 2Q26.

12-month price target raised to $20 from $19. It uses a lower market multiple of 17.6x (from 22.6x) and higher downside/base/upside relative P/E multiples of 35%/40%/45% (from 25%/30%/35%), reflecting less downside risk as the Consumer First Formula strategy progresses.
Risk-reward: downside $13 (25% probability, -31%), base $20 (50%, +6%), upside $27 (25%, +45%), probability-weighted average $20.

market_movers.rationale: Underlying business remains under pressure and GS does not expect a return to growth this year. Price target raised to $20 from $19 on a lower market multiple and higher relative P/E multiples.

earnings_insights: BBWI 3Q26 reported net sales $1,577mn versus FactSet consensus $1,551mn, down 1.1% y/y (2Q26 was -2.3%). Reported 11/19.
BBWI 4Q26 guidance (company): net sales -5.5% to -2.0% y/y versus consensus -2.1%. GS says the guide is at the low end of expectations on sales and below expectations on earnings.
GS 4Q26 estimates (post-print, adjusted): net sales $2,609.3mn (old $2,639.9mn), gross margin 42.2% (old 44.3%), EBIT $447.0mn (old $515.3mn), adj. EPS $1.48 (old $1.70).
GS FY26E adj. EPS $2.67 (old $2.73), FY27E $2.69 (old $2.60), FY28E $2.95 (old $2.85), FY29E $3.23. FY26 includes the $80mn tariff refund benefit received in 2Q26.
GS FY26E revenue $7,078.3mn (-2.9% y/y), gross margin 42.7%, EBIT margin 13.3%.
risk_factors: Underlying business and store traffic remain pressured by inflation-strained consumers and intensifying competition, especially in body care.
4Q gross margin pressure from Canadian tariffs (over 100bps), higher crude oil costs (~100bps) and buying and occupancy deleverage.
4Q sales guide implies sequential deterioration in the top line.

Upside risks to the Sell: faster financial benefit from the new strategy, share gains as consumers respond to the brand, more newness and innovation, easing competition, and higher margins if top-line trends accelerate.
geopolitical: Incremental Canadian tariffs are expected to cut BBWI 4Q gross margin by over 100bps.

tension_points.bull_case: Sales beat consensus ($1,577mn vs $1,551mn) and the y/y decline improved to -1.1% from -2.3%. New franchises (Essentials, Everyday Luxuries, Reserve) and the Amazon and Ulta channels show momentum.
tension_points.bear_case: Traffic remains pressured, body care is declining at a high-single-digit rate, and 4Q guidance implies sequential top-line deterioration with over 200bps of gross margin pressure from tariffs and oil.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained return to positive sales growth or faster financial benefit from the new strategy would undercut the Sell. GS says it does not expect a return to growth this year.

theme_stances.key_argument: The company is in an investment year and the underlying business remains under pressure, so it is too early to signal an inflection.
theme_stances.evidence: too early to signal an inflection in the overall business
